title: a-build-discovery-re-enters-the-chain
intention: When building one ticket discovers another needs building, that discovery re-enters the build chain as a new ticket rather than being lost in conversation.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM, from the voyage that bore this. Building one-owner-for-the-instance-address, two import allowlists refused the new module. I widened both in place, each with a dated comment, and sailed on. Neither file appears anywhere in that voyage's chain — not in the survey's holdings or absences, not in a decompose piece, not in the triage order, not in a validate criterion. So two decisions about what the verdict path and the librarian proof may reach were made inside a build, recorded nowhere the chain can see, and discovered only because the voyage's own criteria were read at the close. The next person to reason about those allowlists reads a widening whose deciding argument lives in a commit message. That is the same shape as live trouble #1 (cairn.tools.base.nest entering the inspector's allowlist with no dated comment at all) — AN UNMADE DECISION WEARING A PASSING SWEEP — and it is what step 8 of I-prebuild-cognition-compiles has said should not happen since 2026-07-19.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy; until it is, it is a tracked debt. The rule already exists in prose: I-prebuild-cognition-compiles step 8 (PROPOSED 2026-07-19), 'Build spawns children: a change can reveal hidden sub-problems, which re-enter as new nodes at step 4', citing MAP.md:44 'build -> deconstruct is the universal shape'. That intention's own why names this exact conversion as its aim: 'it turns the step from a discipline the model must remember into physics it cannot skip (Law 4).' Secondarily Law 1 — a discovery answered inline is an answered question that never became structure.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the tooth is armed at the crossing out of BUILDME and its finding is a named list a reader can adjudicate. WRONG-INTENT if it turns out to measure the chain's PROSE HABITS rather than re-entry. HORIZON: run the detector against the last five closed claimed voyages. KILL CONDITION: if more than roughly one named file in five turns out to have been chain-licensed in a way the substring test could not see, the detector is noise at a gate. VACUITY CONDITION, and it is the half that matters more: an all-empty run across five voyages is a RED, not a pass — a tooth that has only ever reported empty has not been shown to grip.

children: none, because this node is a single tooth at a single crossing and does not split — the detector, its exclusions, and its berth are not separately provable.
how: THE DETECTOR: a file the build MODIFIED that is named NOWHERE in the chain's own berths (survey holdings/absences, decompose pieces, triage order, validate criteria) is a discovery that never re-entered. TWO EXCLUSIONS, each by ADDRESS rather than by judgment, so neither is a place someone adjudicates: (1) ADDED files, because a decompose build piece licenses a file whose name cannot exist at chart time; (2) the component's own voyage bookkeeping — history.json, state.json, validations/, intention+why.json — because those are written BY the crossing, and counting them would make every voyage dirty by construction. THE FINDING IS A NAMED LIST OF FILES, never a count: a count without its sites is precisely the claim this family of ticket exists to stop being made.

watchme.trigger: Each heartbeat pulse of base's shim — an event that already fires, so the probe invents no clock. It reads closed voyages only: the chart berths under ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/ and git name-status per voyage, both artifacts that already exist. Fires when any closed voyage's finding is non-empty, and fires SEPARATELY when the scan examined ZERO voyages — an empty corpus reports zero unchartered edits, indistinguishable from a clean history at exactly the moment the probe has stopped working.
watchme.enough: MEASURABLE HALF, enforced: the detector has run against at least five closed claimed voyages AND has named at least one file across them. The second clause is not decoration — a tooth that has only ever reported empty would clear this watch by never working. DECLARED DEBT: the adjudication half — whether each named file was really an inline answer rather than a chain-licensed edit the substring test could not see — is a human read and nothing automates it. So `enough` clears on non-vacuity and hands adjudication to the consumer, said out loud in the module rather than hidden in a threshold.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the NAMED FILES per voyage — never a bare count or rate — plus the number of voyages examined and both exclusion counts, so a reader can tell a clean history from a scan that excluded everything.

in: the detector, its two exclusions, and its berth
arming it at the emit chokepoint's crossing out of BUILDME, both directions
a proof whose teeth are shown to GRIP: a seeded chain naming every touched file must produce an EMPTY finding, and a seeded voyage with a known inline edit must NAME it
out: REPAIRING the two allowlist widenings this detector names — whether they stand is Akien's ruling, already at his gate from the one-owner-for-the-instance-address kick-back, and a tooth that also fixes what it finds is a tooth nobody can read
checking a decompose piece's file list against the survey berth — a real sibling defect, one stage earlier, and blind to anything discovered after decompose closed
any measure of a build-time CLAIM that produced no edit — this tooth is downstream of the claim and cannot see one
a standalone corpus sweep or any new collector — the check rides a crossing the chokepoint already owns and gates

notes: THE RECURSION IS REAL AND IS THE SHARPEST TEST THIS NODE GETS: this ticket is itself a child spawned by the one-owner-for-the-instance-address BUILD, re-entering as a new node — step 8's shape observed from inside it — and its own crossing out of BUILDME will be the first thing its own tooth measures.

THE QUESTION THAT BORE THIS, answered plainly: neither a bug to fix nor a rule for the survey door. The survey packet's five absences all carried rigorous, explicitly-complete measures. The truncated census happened during BUILDME, where no absence discipline exists at all — so the survey gate would never have seen the case.
